html:
The Marubo are a Panoan people of the upper Ituí and Curuçá rivers in the Javari Valley of western Amazonas, Brazil, near the border with Peru. They live in large communal houses (malocas) and farm, fish and hunt in the forest.

Rubber tappers reached the Javari around 1900, during the rubber boom, bringing violence and epidemics, and the Marubo regrouped in the headwaters. Since 2001 they have lived within the Vale do Javari Indigenous Land, one of the largest in Brazil, with the Matsés, the Kulina Pano, the Korubo and several groups that avoid all contact.
